facts.statement: MVC 5 binds a parameter under its [Bind(Prefix)], else under its own name.
MVC 5 falls back to the unprefixed keys only for a parameter with no [Bind(Prefix)].
MVC 5 binds only the members a parameter's [Bind] includes and does not exclude.
MVC 5 finds a prefix in a key equal to it ignoring case, so a key named like the parameter keeps every key under the parameter's name.
MVC 5 keys a member by its CLR name, and no attribute of MVC 5 renames it.
MVC 5 binds a member as a single value whenever the request holds a value at its exact key, an object member included.
MVC 5 converts an empty or white-space value to null for any type before any converter runs.
MVC 5 writes a null into a member whose type admits null, over its start.
MVC 5 creates a List for a member declared IEnumerable<>, ICollection<> or IList<>, and no other collection interface.
facts.expect: genericTypeDefinition == typeof(IEnumerable<>) || genericTypeDefinition == typeof(ICollection<>) || genericTypeDefinition == typeof(IList<>)

facts.statement: MVC 5 binds repeated keys into a new collection it creates for the member's declared type.
MVC 5 clears the collection a list member starts with and adds the bound items to it, which an array refuses.
MVC 5 ends a list at the first index the request holds no key under.
MVC 5 converts each repeated value of a list of scalars on its own, so an empty one is a null item.
MVC 5 binds an enum from text by Enum.Parse ignoring case.
MVC 5 binds a flags enum from comma-separated names.
On net10 the antiforgery token is read from the header RequestVerificationToken and the form field __RequestVerificationToken by default.

facts.expect: core-antiforgery-placement: [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] answers a JSON body with the token in the header 200; a URL-encoded body with it in its field 200; a multipart body with it in its field 200; a JSON body with it in a member 400; no token 400
